question: On FEVER claim verification with the page given, does a one-hidden-layer MLP outperform multinomial logistic regression on the same TF-IDF features, measured by macro-F1 on held-out Wikipedia pages?
claim: The one-hidden-layer MLP outperforms multinomial logistic regression on FEVER claim verification with the page given, on the same TF-IDF features, measured by macro-F1 on held-out Wikipedia pages.
hypothesis: The MLP outperforms by a small margin, under 0.03 macro-F1, with a page-unit confidence interval that may include zero. Pilot on the validation split (2026-10-15): the MLP scored below logistic regression by 0.026 mean over three seeds under the declared stopping rule; the pilot therefore predicts the hypothesis is not supported.
decision_rule: Supported when the 95% page-unit percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean (over seeds) MLP-minus-logreg macro-F1 difference on the test split excludes 0 in the MLP's favor (lower bound > 0); otherwise not established.
primary_metric: macro-F1, sklearn.metrics.f1_score(average='macro'), label order SUPPORTS, REFUTES, NOT ENOUGH INFO
unit: page: the claim's primary page; the split and the bootstrap both use it

data.dataset: FEVER v1.0, fever.ai claim files and wiki-pages.zip, pinned by SHA-256 in scripts/get_data.py

evidence.rule: top-k sentences of the primary page by TF-IDF cosine to the claim, fitted on the training split

features.blocks: claim block, evidence block, overlap count and cosine standardized with training mean and std; claim-only baseline receives the claim block alone

training.early_stopping: validation log loss; the weights of the best validation-loss epoch are restored

logreg.chosen_by: mean validation macro-F1 over seeds 0, 1, 2 across the grid

mlp.chosen_by: mean validation macro-F1 over seeds 0, 1, 2 across the grid

bootstrap.method: percentile; one draw takes 615 pages with replacement and scores every seed's pair of systems on the same pages, then averages the per-seed differences
bootstrap.secondary: claim-unit interval reported as one line; per-seed page-unit intervals reported

sizing.source: pilot on the validation split, 616 pages

baselines.majority_class: training majority (SUPPORTS) for every test claim
baselines.claim_only: logreg with the chosen logreg decay on the claim block alone, seed 0
baselines.library_check: sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression, C = 1, on the same features (validation only)

checks.quantity: Vectorizer vocabulary fitted on the training set only
checks.condition: no term that occurs only in the validation or test set is in it

checks.quantity: Torch logistic regression against sklearn LogisticRegression, same features, validation macro-F1

checks.condition: validation macro-F1 at chance: within 0.05 of 1/3 (uniform) or of the majority-class macro-F1 (prior only)
the same seed reproduces the saved validation metrics

test_set_read.rule: once, by run.py test, after this file is committed; run.py refuses to run twice
test_set_read.reads: 2 systems x 3 seeds + 1 claim-only baseline = 7 predict_proba calls in one invocation

secondary_analyses: per-class precision, recall, F1, support; confusion matrices; accuracy
generalization gap per system and seed
distance to the majority-class and claim-only baselines
